fix_commit.message: BIO_send/recvmmsg(): Pass msgs_processed to the return callback
fix_commit.author: Tomas Mraz

findings.title: NULL pointer dereference in legacy BIO callback path for BIO_sendmmsg/BIO_recvmmsg
findings.message: When BIO_sendmmsg() and BIO_recvmmsg() invoke the BIO_CB_*MMSG|BIO_CB_RETURN callback via bio_call_callback(), they pass a hard-coded NULL for the `processed` output parameter, while passing the actual number of processed messages (`ret`) as the `inret` argument. Prior to this commit, `inret` was always hard-coded to 0 for the RETURN callback, so the legacy-callback branch in bio_call_callback() (`if (inret > 0 && (oper & BIO_CB_RETURN) ...) { if (*processed > INT_MAX) ... inret = *processed; }`) could never execute, since inret was never >0. This commit changed the call so that `inret` is now the real `ret` value returned by the underlying bsendmmsg/brecvmmsg method, which can legitimately be >0 whenever any messages were sent/received. When a legacy (non-_ex) BIO callback is installed on the BIO via BIO_set_callback(), and BIO_sendmmsg()/BIO_recvmmsg() successfully process at least one message, bio_call_callback() will now dereference the `processed` pointer (`*processed > INT_MAX`) even though NULL was passed for it, causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash (reported by Stanislav Fort, Aisle Research).
findings.suggestion: Pass the actual `msgs_processed` pointer (instead of NULL) as the `processed` argument to bio_call_callback() for the BIO_CB_SENDMMSG|BIO_CB_RETURN and BIO_CB_RECVMMSG|BIO_CB_RETURN calls, so that the legacy-callback compatibility path in bio_call_callback() can safely write/read through it whenever inret (the return value) is greater than zero.

ground_truth.root_cause: The BIO_sendmmsg/BIO_recvmmsg 'return' callback invocations pass NULL for the processed-message-count out-parameter while also passing a nonzero 'inret' value, and the internal legacy-callback shim (bio_call_callback) unconditionally dereferences that pointer whenever inret > 0 for BIO_CB_RETURN callback invocations that aren't BIO_CB_CTRL. The introducing commit changed inret from a permanently-zero placeholder to the genuine (potentially positive) return value without also supplying a valid processed pointer, re-activating a previously dead/safe code path with an invalid NULL argument.
